name: Final quest state against the request over the quest operation cases
purpose: In-memory quest state after the run over the quest_ops cases, a share held out: the right tool with the right arguments, every step of a multi-step request, no write on an ambiguous or sharing message, a delete that was not confirmed leaves the experiment in place, no unrequested write Read in this direction: maximise how exactly the final quest state matches the request; minimise unrequested writes, duplicate records, steps left undone in a multi-step request, and tokens and planner turns spent per change. The pre-route and the planner path pass the same cases and the pre-route spends fewer tokens, but by less than a sampled run's margin (the previous recording differed by less), so it is a tie, not a win on spend or quality.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.

name: Outcome reporting correctness across deep runners
purpose: Per runner, the same scenarios through the subprocess runner and the ACP runner with the outside peer faked at its process edge: how each outcome is reported back (met, silent no-op, paused with a decision id, partial or crashed, missing binary), and no scenario raises (deep_runner). Secondary arm: the done-standard contract the goal loop applies whichever runner ran it (deep_run): met-versus-limit, stop rules, escalation and resume markers, the headless prompt Read in this direction: maximise goals met within the turn and cost bound; minimise cost per success and silent failures, and report every outcome in one common shape whichever runner ran. Cost per success is not seen: the runner scenarios script the process edge, so no tokens or dollars are produced, and the two runners tie on the contract. The stream_json runner is not scored by these scenarios, so its value (receive-input-mid-run measures with cost per run as the guard) is not shown here.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.

name: Hand-offs a person keeps per unit of cost and time
purpose: from the goals the judge handled: maximise the share of its verdicts that a person did not reassign or reverse (value), at a cost per goal below the cost of the reassignment it avoids and a verdict time inside goal creation that the person does not notice. Counted from the host's reassignment records, never from the model's words; a lane that keeps no such record cannot read it.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set or arm exists yet. Reassignment is a late and noisy signal, a person may keep a wrong verdict, and a goal that is never reassigned looks right.

name: Account-state consistency across scripted sessions
purpose: Measures whether what the AI says about the person's account is true when said and consistent across a session. Read in this direction: maximise state claims that match the store at reply time; allow no contradiction and no repeated or re-proposed change; minimise reads per turn. Its cases include questions about how to use the app, answered from the product documentation, and claims about what the AI can do in the app.
record: Per implementation on the same scripted sessions: the share of state claims matching the store at reply time, contradictions per session, repeated or re-proposed changes, and reads per turn; and the share of app-usage questions answered correctly and in-app capability claims that are true; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. It needs a disposable host account and the host's real operations, so it cannot run wholly offline; it sees only changes the script makes, not concurrent ones; a claim extractor decides what counts as a state claim.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the card_and_reads offline arm of act_as_the_body runs the whole case set with no model call]
